drafts.walkScript: At line 71 a gust of wind comes 'over the field'. Line 73 says it was a place 'where he might lose his balance'. So the wind has just reminded him that he could fall. Lines 74 and 75 say he 'was not to be tempted to watch' the dragonfly. He keeps 'steadily on, a foot at a time', at line 75.

Line 40 has Sebastian point 'to his own head and then to hers'. Line 41 says his signs and nods mean 'I have got it all safe for you'. The words 'for you' show the thing he is keeping is hers. Line 42 shows what it was: 'her old straw hat'. He is not asking her to point at anything herself.

Line 31 says the other end has 'proper netting'. Line 33 says this end is 'two jumpers and the air between them'. So this goal has no net at all. Yet line 34 uses 'still', and line 35 has them say 'in the net'. Lines 36 and 37 say nobody has ever pointed out that 'there isn't one'.

Line 63 has Nag tell how 'The great God Brahm put his mark' on cobras. Line 64 ends 'Look, and be', and line 65 finishes 'afraid!' So the mark is shown to scare, as his own words say. Lines 67 and 68 say Rikki-tikki 'was afraid for the minute'. Spreading the hood is how he shows it, not why.

Lines 38 and 39 have Mrs Farrell say the word 'again'. Line 39 goes on: 'that will be about the fountain'. Line 39 calls the fountain 'ages ago'. Line 40 says 'everybody has moved on from it', so Dilan thinks it is finished. Mum coming early, at line 36, is not what the word is about.

Line 39 says Jo 'wanted' to cry her anger away, but wanting is not doing. Line 40 calls tears 'unmanly', and at line 41 she 'couldn't quite forgive yet'. So at line 41 she 'winked hard' to stop the tears coming. Lines 42 and 43 have her say 'she doesn't deserve to be forgiven'. The tears stay in, and the words that come out are harsh.

Line 54 says he looks about 'as a man looks who thinks on flight'. Here 'flight' means running away, so he is searching for an escape. His step trembles on line 53 and his hand shakes on line 55. Nothing in these lines says he is ill, so the shaking comes from fear. The red and white face is how he looks, not what he feels.

Lines 43 and 44 show Grandad swat something away 'without much interest'. So the thing passing his ear does not stop him. Line 45 says 'Then he stops. He is listening to the door.' Line 46 has him say 'Oh, hang on', as if a sound has caught him. Listening shows a sound from the door has made him stop.
